## My Reasoning

I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn. That is what this land is good for, that is what the collectors come to buy, and that is what I know how to do. I am 62 now, my back is not what it was, so I need to keep things manageable.

I have about 10 mu of land. Same land, two seasons — winter wheat then summer maize. I have done this rotation for forty years. The wheat stubble helps the corn soil, the corn stubble gets chopped up before wheat planting. It works.

For wheat, I will buy the improved seed from the county seed station — the same variety I used last two years, good yield, not too tall so it does not lodge. The government seed subsidy helps with cost. I will hire the tractor neighbor to do rotary tillage before seeding. I always irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. That is what my experience tells me is enough without wasting pump money.

For corn I always use hybrid seed —郑单958 or whatever the station has on offer. Yields are clearly better than before. I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June, no tillage needed, saves time and my joints appreciate it. Summer rains usually help but I pump once or twice if July turns dry or at filling stage.

Fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer as base and urea on top. Heavy enough for decent yield. I do not skimp here — thin fertilizer means thin harvest, I learned that the hard way when I was young.
